bib.title: Diverse And Private Synthetic Datasets Generation for RAG evaluation: A multi-agent framework

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Diverse And Private Synthetic Datasets Generation for RAG evaluation: A multi-agent framework", Ilias Driouich, Hongliu Cao, Eoin Thomas (all AMADEUS France). Venue: TRUST-AI, European Workshop on Trustworthy AI, part of ECAI 2025, October 2025, Bologna (workshop paper, CC BY 4.0). arXiv 2508.18929 (Aug 2025). File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/driouich-2025-diverse-private-synthetic-datasets-generation.pdf

COVERAGE: 29,014 of 29,014 chars read, all 7 pages including references. Nothing skipped. There is no appendix and no limitations section. Figure 1 is an image: I have only its caption, not the bar values. The text gives some values.

TARGET NOTE: generative-ai/08-eval/notes/03-eval-datasets.md (7,616 words). Best fit is "### Synthetic data done right" (line 95), which sits under "## Where tasks come from".
- Already covered there: generating along dimensions and tuples; self-preference; synthetic-only suites; Perez et al. on diversity lost when pushing toward failures, tracked by self-BLEU and unique n-grams; the BigToM template approach. Production logs are flagged only as "Consent and PII" in the sources table (line 81).
- Lacking: (a) embedding-clustering of the source corpus, with a sample drawn per cluster, as a way to get topical coverage for corpus-grounded QA; (b) masking PII in the source before generating QA, so private data does not enter the eval set; (c) a pairwise LLM-judge diversity rating and an embedding-similarity diversity score. Neither the note nor references.md mentions Driouich or 2508.18929. The ledger has no entry, which I found with grep only.
- Alternatives: 07-evaluating-rag-and-grounding.md covers RAGAS but not dataset generation. It could take a one-line pointer. The note's "Where tasks come from" table row for production logs (PII) is a second hook. The best home is still 03, "Synthetic data done right", plus a short privacy sentence.
- Suggested classification: sharpens for the clustering and diversity idea, with weak evidence. The privacy-masking evidence is thin (see LIMITS).

CORE CLAIM: A LangGraph pipeline of three agents builds RAG eval QA sets. (1) A Diversity agent runs k-means on chunk embeddings and picks representative samples per cluster. (2) A Privacy agent detects and pseudonymizes PII and writes a privacy report. (3) A QA curation agent generates n QA pairs per private sample and writes a QA report. The authors claim it beats RagasGen and direct prompting on diversity and masks PII "robustly".

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Diversity: the pipeline scores higher than two baselines on a GPT-4.1 1–10 rating at every size.
 number: at n=10, 7.8 vs 7.0 (RagasGen) vs 6.2 (DirPmpt). At n=100, 9.0 vs 8.1 vs 7.6.
 setup: input is one document, the EU AI Act. Generator GPT-4o, temperature 0. Judge GPT-4.1 sees pairs of sets and rates semantic variety, topical coverage and phrasing on 1–10. Set sizes 10/25/50/75/100. A single number per cell: no runs, no variance, no n of documents. RagasGen is an evolutionary baseline in the style of Evol-Instruct and RAGAS. DirPmpt is few-shot GPT-4o prompting with handcrafted instructions.
 quote: "The LLM-as-a-Judge scores (GPT-4.1) rise from 7.8 at 10 samples to 9 at 100 samples"
 where: p.4–5, Table 1 (Section 4.2.4)
2. Diversity as measured by embedding similarity: the table's numbers do not support the paper's reading (see INCONSISTENCIES).
 number: Ours -0.36 → -0.15; RagasGen -0.40 → -0.33; DirPmpt -0.45 → -0.33 (n=10 → 100).
 setup: CosineSimilaritytoDiversity (Gao & Zhang 2024, VRSD), "inverts the average pairwise cosine similarity of sentence embeddings". Embedding model for this metric is not stated.
 quote: "lower values indicate greater semantic spread"
 where: Section 4.2.3
3. Privacy agent entity accuracy on three AI4Privacy datasets (PII, PWI, PHI), concatenated into long paragraphs.
 number: best labels are JOBTYPE 0.94, LASTNAME 0.91, DISABILITYSTATUS 0.91; GENDER is 0.83 on PHI, 0.88 on PWI and 0.83 on PII.
 setup: privacy agent is GPT-4.1 at temperature 0. "Accuracy" is never defined. Only the top labels are listed in the text; the rest is in Figure 1. There is no baseline such as Presidio or a regex tool, no recall/precision split, no run count.
 quote: "most labels achieving accuracies between 0.75 and 0.90"
 where: p.6, Section 4.3.2 and Figure 1
4. Pipeline config. The agents' models are GPT-4o for diversity and QA, and GPT-4.1 for privacy. Embeddings are text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dimensions. Chunks are 256 tokens. k is chosen by "intra-cluster distance scores".
 quote: "Input documents were preprocessed into chunks of 256 tokens before applying 𝑘-means clustering."
 where: Section 4.1
5. Dataset stats (as printed, see INCONSISTENCIES): PWI "1800 / 451 / 3.99", PHI "1700 / 422 / 4.02", PII "1600 / 591 / 2.71". where: Table 2.

LIMITS (stated): the future work section concedes no test of resilience to privacy attacks: "Future work will also include rigorous evaluation of the framework's resilience to privacy attacks". It also notes that the privacy agent works from a static entity list.
LIMITS (unstated):
- No evaluation of QA quality: correctness, answerability, or groundedness. There is no human check and no run of any RAG system on the generated set.
- Diversity is tested on one document. The privacy test uses synthetic AI4Privacy text, and no run tests the two together, so the QA output is never checked for leaked PII.
- The same OpenAI family generates the data and (GPT-4.1) judges diversity. A judge that prefers its own family's output is a risk, and the paper does not address it.
- No ablation, so the gain from clustering versus the other parts is unknown.
- No baseline for privacy. Pseudonymizing is not a privacy guarantee, and no differential-privacy claim is made.
- Rating gaps of about 1 point at a single run have no confidence interval.
- How representative samples are chosen is unspecified, as are n QA per sample and the prompts. The paper has no code link.
- The "diversity grows with set size" trend is partly built in, since more samples cover more clusters.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES
- Table 1 cosine column: the paper says lower values mean more spread, yet "Ours" is the least negative (closest to zero) at every size, so on that rule it is the least diverse. The text then says "less negative (closer to zero)" means more dissimilar. The two statements contradict each other. The metric's sign convention is also unclear. The cosine column does not back the claim "outperforms ... in all evaluated settings". Only the GPT-4.1 judge column clearly favors the method.
- The "Ours" cosine trend (-0.36 → -0.15) moves toward zero as the set grows, and the baselines converge to the same value (-0.33 for both at n=100).
- Table 2: "Dataset length (sentences)" and "Total entities number" appear swapped. 451 × 3.99 ≈ 1800, 422 × 4.02 ≈ 1696 and 591 × 2.71 ≈ 1601, so the 1800/1700/1600 figures are entity counts and the 451/422/591 figures are sentence counts. Read as printed, 451 entities over 1,800 sentences would be 0.25 per sentence, not 3.99.
- Text says "most labels ... 0.75 and 0.90" while naming labels at 0.91 and 0.94; only the top labels are reported, so selective reporting is possible.
- Text calls the datasets "PII-Masking-200K, PWI-Masking-200K, PHI-Masking-200K" but uses only 1,600–1,800 samples each. The sampling is not explained.
- Abstract says "robust privacy masking", but accuracies of 0.83–0.91 would leave roughly 1 in 10 entities unmasked on some labels.

BUILDS ON: RAGAS (Es et al. 2024, evolutionary question generation); Evol-Instruct; Cao, Driouich, Singh, Thomas 2025 (multi-agent LLM judge, arXiv:2504.02867); Zeng et al. 2024 (privacy issues in RAG) and Zeng et al. 2025 (pure synthetic data for RAG privacy, arXiv:2406.14773); Gao & Zhang 2024 (VRSD, diversity metric); Tang et al. 2023 and Xie et al. 2024 (differential-privacy synthetic data); Yu et al. 2024 (attributed data generation for diversity); Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Huang et al. 2023 and Qi et al. 2024 (RAG extraction attacks); AI4Privacy datasets (Hugging Face); LangGraph.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Algorithm 1 (p.3), the three-stage flow: k-means into clusters, representative samples, PII pseudonymization, then QA generation with two reports. It is a clear pipeline outline for a note. Figure 1 (p.7, "Privacy agent accuracy per entity type across the PHI, PWI, and PII datasets") is not worth reusing because there is no baseline.

CODE: none in the paper. The only code-like item is Algorithm 1 (pseudocode).

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean. There are no embedded instructions. The "Ada 3" label for text-embedding-3-small is the paper's own and is misleading (Ada is an older model). The abstract's "extensive experiments" means one document for diversity and three synthetic PII sets for privacy. The "mentions in 4.1 that the QA agent uses 'advanced prompting techniques'" claim has no detail in the text.
